goal: Repair bounded zero-commit batch plan reconfirmation through the existing native authority and shared runtime, preserving lineage, exact completed-child evidence and serial progress without recovering the original failed live batch.

acceptance.assertion: Implement docs/specs/batch-plan-reconfirmation.spec.md: only a fresh native-confirmed capability may replace the plan binding of a nonterminal, zero-commit batch whose ordered tasks/Slices/dependencies, branch/base and current HEAD are unchanged. Reconstruct the old digest from canonical baseline Intents; require an actual monotonic revised, same-goal/owner child that is done in its exact local run with matching Intent, fresh QA/required Review and intact reviewed delivery. Pending children remain unchanged. Atomically compare expected state bytes and recheck binding/evidence/clock/claim before replacing only digest and confirmed authorization timing/budget, retaining all progress and limits. Shared entry paths reconcile settlement, commit once and continue without replaying Enrollment or Assurance. Real temporary Kernel/Git/public-entry tests prove this and refusal/replay behavior; corrupted digests, topology/HEAD/commit drift, ambiguous/stale/foreign evidence, mixed dirty work, forged/expired authority and declined/cancelled or drifting confirmation fail closed with raw-byte zero-write controls. Preserve existing negative and same-digest behavior, both Host seams and generated bundle parity. No repair of the original pi-batch-acceptance batch, S1 execution, manual authority/state edits, new schema or weakened commit guard. Typecheck and focused delivery checks must pass before Review; fixture evidence does not certify live user interaction.
